cards.body:
## Summary
An answer to a card holds the daemon-wide write lock for as long as the card's action runs. For a connector or MCP card that action is an outbound HTTP call of up to 20 s, so every page's manifest, every other card's answer and every spoken yes or no waits behind one email being sent. The guard is keyed wrong: the entity it protects is one card, not the daemon.

## Description
`decide` (decisions.py:77) wraps `lane.answer_decision` in `daemon.writing()`. ADR 0141 kept that lock as the short write lock for 'the milliseconds the write takes'. For a host card that is true: the replay only returns an execute instruction. For a core or connector card it is not: `answer_decision` calls `gate.run_tool`, which runs the executor in place (hooks.py:377). A Gmail send or an MCP `tools/call` has a 20 s request timeout (vault.py:76, mcp/client.py:53). For all of that time `POST /manifest` cannot merge, though the shell sends one for every tab with an admitted origin (ADR 0065). A tab opened while she sends an email therefore has no tools, and its next turn is refused with 'Open the app this is about'. A second card cannot be answered either, and the voice gateway's spoken answer goes through the same `decide`.

The lock is not needed for correctness. Two answers to one card are already settled in the table: `resolve` is a conditional UPDATE on `pending` (approvals.py:494) and `consume` is conditional on `consumed_at IS NULL` (approvals.py:538, ADR 0038). The catalog replaces an origin in one assignment and the pin is a policy-object swap. The vault single-flights token refresh per connector (vault.py:487). Turns already run connector tools from several conversations at once with no daemon lock.

The move (concurrency-guards / guard-key-design: 'unrelated work queues behind one guard'): the daemon gains a keyed lock map, the shape `ThreadLocks` already has (entries counted and dropped when the last holder leaves). `decide` takes the lock for its card id and leaves `writing()` alone. The critical section stays whole for that card, from resolve through replay to consume, so no check-to-use window opens (critical-section-across-a-suspension). Two answers to one card still run one after the other, and the loser reads the winner's settled row. `writing()` stays for the manifest merge, its one remaining multi-object act. The connector acts in daemon/connectors.py also hold `writing()` across `vault.probe` and `connect_token`. That file belongs to cli-and-wiring; this card names it as the follow-up and does not edit it.

## Flow
- write the slow-connector fixture (a ConnectorPort whose call sleeps) and acceptance cases 1-3, then watch them fail at about 3 s
- generalize the counted lock map in server.py (ThreadLocks becomes a keyed lock map used for conversations and for cards; `AthenaDaemon.card(approval_id)` is a context manager)
- decide takes `daemon.card(approval_id)` in place of `daemon.writing()`; update the docstrings of writing() and decisions.py
- guard cases 4-8 stay green; ADR amending 0141; CHANGELOG line

## Expected impact
Approving a send no longer freezes the daemon for up to 20 s. Tabs opened meanwhile get their tools, and other cards and spoken answers return at once. A whole class closes: no route holds the global lock across an executor. Could break: an executor that relied on being alone in the daemon. None of the shipped executors does, because turns already run them concurrently.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - an answer to a card never waits on another card's action
Before: 0 of 3 timing cases pass (each waits the fake executor's 3 s); guards 4-8 pass
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases on a real socket
Result: better
Gate: none

cards.body:
## Summary
Every card in the inbox looks answerable. Some cannot run: the app is switched off, the page whose tools it names has gone, or the connector is disconnected. The person finds out only after pressing Approve, from a 409 and a sentence written after the fact (ADR 0060). The daemon already has every fact needed to say so first: the gate's own rules, the catalog, the pins and the vault. This card makes the inbox say, per card, whether it will run, why not, and the one act that fixes it.

## Description
`GET /decisions` (decisions.py:190) returns rows only. The approve path then judges each card under `_decision_ctx` (decisions.py:152) with `Policy.authorize` (policy.py:166), after `catalog.get` (browser_lane.py:321). Each of those is a pure read. The preflight runs those same reads for every listed row, under the same context the replay will build. It never resolves, consumes or writes. Each row gains `will_run` and `blocked: {reason, rule, sentence, remedy}`. `reason` is a member of ERROR_REASONS. `rule` is the policy rule or `tools_gone`. `remedy` is one act the surface can offer as a single press: `switch_on` an origin, `open_app` at the pinned page origin, or `reconnect` a connector. The optional `?disabled_origins=` query carries the shell's switched-off list, parsed and capped as POST /run parses it. The verdict is not a second gate. It is the gate's own rules evaluated early, and the agreement cases pin that the prediction equals the replay's outcome.

hitl-approval / review-queues: 'every pending decision, one surface, enough context to decide in place'. An item that needs a trip elsewhere gets decided blind. Here the trip is the refusal itself.

The surface work (the card shows 'Won't run: Ledger is switched off - Switch on' and holds Approve until then) is the desktop's follow-up and is not in this write set. The daemon side is complete and testable offline.

## Flow
- write cases 1-4 and 8 against the conftest daemon (host card, drop_origin, a connector port marked not live) and watch them fail on the missing keys
- add `_preflight(daemon, row, disabled)` in decisions.py: build the context with `_decision_ctx`, get the entry from the catalog (gone means tools_gone), call `gate.policy.authorize`, and map the rule to a sentence and a remedy
- decisions() parses `disabled_origins` from the query (comma list, MAX_DISABLED_ORIGINS, refused whole) and adds the two keys to each row
- guards 5-7; ADR; CHANGELOG line

## Expected impact
An approve that cannot work stops costing a press, a refusal and, after a reload, a lost card (ADR 0060 consequences). The person sees the fix in place. The inbox and the gate cannot disagree, because one set of rules answers both. Could break: a slow catalog or policy read on a 200-row inbox. Both are in-memory and O(rows).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a card's inbox row predicts its replay's outcome and names the fix
Before: 0 of 5 behaviour cases pass (no will_run or blocked keys); guards 5-7 pass
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases
Result: better
Gate: none

riders.checked: Read face.py, face_helper/{__init__,main,probe}.py, motion.py head and signatures, visemes.py signatures, and kokoro.py's _faced and synthesize_face callers. Hypotheses traced: a restart re-probes motion every time; a flap of two misses then a kill while the probe saturates the CPU; per-sentence re-probe. No card: each is S, impact under 7, or needs torch or a GPU to show its effect, so it cannot be an offline acceptance case.
